ABB 7095MP. 13.9.101 A ABB Azipod Oy/TJB 11.9.98 1/3 Azipod mounting and demounting instructions Refering documents 7095MP. 13.1.100 Assembly Drawing 7095MP.40.1.102 Air channel Arrangement 7095MP.20.5.100 Steering Mechanical Arrangement Specimas 16.6.98 Maintenance Instruction For Specimas Vertical Collector (Slipring Unit KK450 140 3200/103SD.423S with svivel 3x1”) Special tools needed Flange lift device Upper radial slewing bearing assembly tool Pinion assembly tool Transport platform Side lifting lugs 4 pcs Starting point The Azipod rudder propeller unit has been equipped with flange lift device, steering lower radial slewing bearing and seal pack of lower radial bearing with counter ring.The Azipod unit has been transported just below the hole of the steering vertical line and connected through the ship to the lifting crane. The weight of the Azipod unit is approximately 34 tons.Pod cap, the propeller and the shaft shield with the rope cutter has been mounted.The pod service hatch has also been mounted . In the Azipod room the outer parts of the air cooling with the coolers and cooling fans has been mounted in to their final position. Only the slipring inner foundation and the outer foundation, the slipring unit itself and the channel from the slipring unit has been left outside. Also outside are turning gear wheel with screws and the L-ring. Procedures 1. The steering upper radial slewing seals (3 pcs) are to be mounted in to the steering block so that the lowest lip seal is working against outer pressure from sea water and the upper two lip seals are going to work against oil pressure from inside.Spacer ring 4mm is under the most upper seal for lip support. Special care has to be taken of to make sure that the springs of the lip seals are properly at their own place after lifting of the rudder propeller unit. 2. The upper radial slewing bearing of the steering is to be mounted with bearing assembly tool. Loctite glue and the screws Ml0x50 are used for the securing the bearing. Because of the tight fitting the total force of the mounting is approximately 100 tons. On the lower edge of the bearing there are slots for lubrication which have to be pointed to the corresponding holes on the inner cylindrical surface of the assembly block. 3. The lower axial slewing bearing sectors are to be mounted to the bottom of the gear wheel space. 4. The separate pinion bearing housings are to be mounted with their O-rings and screws to the bottom of the gear wheel space.

Aim **■»» 2/3 5. The last checks are to be carried out before lifting the rudder propeller unit, Especially the flange lifting device has to be mounted carefully. 6. Lifting is started slowly pointing the steering cylinder carefully into the hole of the block. Some horizontal forces are needed to get the right line. Special care has to be taken off to make sure that the lip seals are properly at their own place after lifting of the rudder propeller unit. 7. The lower radial seal pack and its fixing ring is to be mounted, when the vertical distance between the ship hull and the Azipod is approximately 120 mm ... 150mm..That is a suitable space for lifting the fixing ring and tightening the screws. 8. The Azipod unit is to be lifted until the lower surface of the flange lift device is setting at 18 mm ±2mm height above the lower axial slewing bearing on the bottom of the gear wheel space. 9. The propeller unit has to be fixed in this point and supported rigidly outside the ship. 10. The flange lifting device can be taken off and lifted outside.The hole of the Azipod top has to be immediately covered carefully for working time.This can be made eg. with tough clothing or felts (Note; that the working time cover clothing is to be taken carefully off during the procedure number 26 and it has to be able to get out via hatches of the inner and outer slipring unit foundations.) Absolutely no any objects may be dropped in to the Azipod because of the obvious damage after electric supply! 1 l.The O-ring seal and the steering gear wheel is to be mounted on to the upper head of the Azipod. The right angle is when the stopper hole on the gear wheel is 45° outside and forward from the vertical steering line.The L-ring with the O-ring seal and screws are to be mounted tightening according to the specific value at the drawing. 12. After this the Azipod can be lowered to the final height and the outside support can be disassembled. 13. The upper axial slewing bearing sectors are to be mounted on to the cover of the gear wheel space. 14. The O-ring seal of the gear wheel cover is to be mounted into its groove, after that the cover will be mounted. This mounting needs a considerable force. 15. The upper two lip seals are to be mounted between the cover and the L-ring. 16. The inner slipring inner foundation is to be mounted to the azipod top. 17. The hose assemblies and fittings are to be mounted to the piping on the upper head of the Azipod unit.The valves in the upper end of the oil transfer tubes are to be secured close. The space for asssembly is especially small.Still extreme care has to be taken to make mounting reliable so that no parts may be left loose!

The Azipod steering locking pin has been mounted to the gear wheel. The shaft shield and the propeller has been removed. The Azipod hull cap has been removed.(3 ton lifting lug has to be welded onto cap) The dismounting equipment has been erected and connected to the thrust bearing and shafting. (The dismounting equipment has to be aligned so that the shaft assembly may differ only ±1.0mm from the line of the dismounting equipment. Procedures 1. The shield of the service hatch below the Azipod hull has to be grinded off and the hatch itself has to be removed. 2. The shaft outboard seal is to be removed 3. The zink anodes are to be grinded off. 4. The hexagon screws M20x80 (12 pcs at dia 570) has to be removed to loosen the propeller bearing housing.The housing is to be attached to the shaft before the shaft assembly removal. 5. The propeller bearing piping and the sensors inside the Azipod has to be disconnected. 6. At the thrust bearing end the piping and the sensor cabling has to be disassembled. 7. The socket screwes M24x75 (24 pcs at dia 1290) has to be removed to loosen the shaft assembly.

Aim #*■»« 2/2 8. The rotor assembly is to be removed slowly.The rotor and stator gap has to be constantly watched to prevent the possible damage.Note! The weight of the shafting assembly in this stage is approximately 15 tons. A At first the support is taken in front by the overhauling tube sliding on a slide surface. The rear end is supported from the thrust bearing to the side girders by rollers. B The out-pulling is proceded by the tacle from the rear rollers. C After the assembly is out enough to see the propeller bearing from side, the support is to be arranget from the propeller bearing to the side girders via rollers. D The assembly has to be lowered carefully to wooden blocks. Bending has to be avoided. Mounting is to be made in reverse order. Note! When mounting the shaft assembly the accuracy of the aligning is to be controlled first when penetrating the rotor into the stator and secondly when penetrating the propeller bearing housing into the hull bore. Adjusting has to be made whenever neccessary.

+49-9721-913832 FAG SW LT-A 583 P02 07.10.98 10:41 AZIPOD 1,5-MW-Drive Description, Mounting and Operating Instructions for Floating bearing / Propeller end as shown in ABB-sketch SK231197 "—x. consisting of: 1 spherical roller bearing FAG 23064K.MB.C4.H50U 1 adapter sleeve FAG 195348 (see sketch SK980333-T1) Description: The floating bearing location at the propeller end features a spherical roller bearing. The particular inherent feature of this bearing type is that outer and inner ring together with the roller and cage assembly can be swivelled around the bearing centre without affecting its function neither in case of rotor shaft deflections nor with inevitable misalignments during shaft alignment. The bearing with its tapered bore is placed on the likewise tapered seat of the adapter sleeve. The spherical roller bearing is driven up its seat by means of a hydraulic nut. It is both mounted and dismounted by the hydraulic method. When the bearing is pressed onto the tapered seat, its inner ring undergoes an elastic expansion. As a consequence, the initial radial clearance is reduced. The inner ring is only expanded to an extent necessary for a tight fit on the shaft. Prior to mounting, the radial clearance has to be measured with a feeler gauge. The correct measuring method and the required clearance reduction are indicated under "Mounting instructions". The bearing is protected by an anti-corrosion oil which does not have to be washed before mounting. *) *) In edition 2 the synthetic oil from Mobil SHC 630 has been replaced by mineral oils from Shell (Omala 220) and Mobil (Mobilgear 630). This change as been considered in the Operating Instructions (see page 6). The mineral oils have been approved by the seal supplier and FAG 22015 3 D1938

Prior to bearing mounting, check if shaft dimensions and tolerances of the mating parts are as specified (see ABB sketch SK231197, and FAG fitter's report). The following equipment must be at hand for mounting (and dismounting): 1 set of feeler gauges for measuring the radial clearance of 0.220 to 0.600 mm 1 connecting piece FAG 118549A-M6 (see sketch SK960602-T1) 1 hydraulic nut FAG RKP320 (see sketch SK970714-T1) 1 hand pump or motor pump (800 bar) with a 4.54 oil container and a high-pressure hose (approx. 2 m long, connecting thread G1/4") for operating the hydraulic nut RKP320 1 hand pump (800 bar) with 1.3-1 oil container and high pressure hose (approx. 2 m long, connecting thread G1/4") for mounting and dismounting the spherical roller bearing (connected via the connecting piece 118549A-M6) 1 special hook spanner HN380/400 (DIN 1810A) for tightening the adapter sleeve nut HM3064H after hydraulic mounting of the spherical roller bearing. 4 ledges with fastening and positioning bolts (see sketch SK980334-T1) for positioning the bearing outer ring relative to the inner ring during mounting on the rotor shaft. 8 hex head bolts SKSB.DIN561-BM12x60-8.8 for slackening the adapter sleeve nut. 1 eye-bolt (DIN 580-M8) for the hydraulic nut RKP320 Bearing mounting has to be carried out with utmost cleanliness and preferably in the following order: Thoroughly clean adapter sleeve seat on the shaft and wipe dry. Thinly oil adapter sleeve O.D. and bearing bore. Slip spherical roller bearing onto the adapter sleeve and screw hydraulic nut onto the adapter sleeve (fully retract annular piston). Note: The maximum stroke of the hydraulic nut is 14 mm. Do not try to extend piston farther. Connect hand pump or motor pump (800 bar, 4.5-I oil container) to the hydraulic nut by means of high-pressure hose (connecting thread G1/4"). Wrap external thread of connecting piece 118549A-M6 with sealing tape. Connect accessories (hand pump, connecting piece, adapter sleeve) as follows: Hand pump (800 bar; 1.3-1 oil container; high-pressure hose, approx. 2 m long, connecting thread G1/4") Connecting piece 118549A-M6 Adapter sleeve 195348 A pressure fluid to be injected between bearing bore and tapered adapter sleeve seat should be a medium viscosity machine oil. For mounting we recommend to use a thin oil having a viscosity of approx. 75 mm2/s at 20 °C (nominal viscosity: 32 mm2/s at 40 °C) which guarantees that the oil will completely escape from the fitting joints after mounting. For hydraulic nut operation, use a machine oil with a viscosity of 46 mm2/s at 40 °C. Pump oil into the hydraulic nut until a close fit between shaft, adapter sleeve and bearing bore has been obtained. Pump oil between the fitting surfaces until it escapes between bearing inner ring and O.D. of the adapter sleeve. Only then actuate pump of the hydraulic nut so that the bearing is slowly driven up the adapter sleeve until the specified radial clearance reduction has been obtained. At the same time pump oil into the fitting joint (bearing bore/sleeve O.D.) via the connecting piece by means of hand pump. The radial clearance reduction for the spherical roller bearing amounts to 250 pm, which corresponds to an axial bearing drive-up of 3.4 +0.2 mm. 22 015 3 DJ1936

After mounting the rotor shaft into the housing, remove the 4 ledges together with the positioning bolts. Prior to putting into service fill in lubricating oil (see operation specification and specifications for the shop test run/drive shaft etc. according to MAL 980306-T1E). Dismounting: Preferably dismount the spherical roller bearing by the hydraulic method. For mounting, a thicker oil (approx. 150 mm^/s at 20 °C; nominal viscosity: 46 mm^/s at 40 °C) can be pumped between the fitting surfaces. If these have been damaged, a thicker gear or cylinder oil with approx. 1150 mrn^/s at 20 °C (nominal viscosity: 320 mm^/s at 40 °C) should be used. +49-9721-913832 FflG SW LT-8 5B1P02 07.10.98 10:19 AZIPOD 1,5-MW-Drive Description, Mounting and Operating Instructions for Thrust Block FAG FKA9360.175934.A consisting of: 1 thrust block housing FAG FKA9360.175934.A 1 spherical roller thrust bearing FAG 29360E.M15SX.M15SZ 1 spherical roller thrust bearing FAG 29352E.M15SX.M15SZ 1 spherical roller bearing FAG 23956MB.C3.M15CX.M15CZ Description The thrust block is equipped with one spherical roller bearing and 2 spherical roller thrust bearings. The spherical roller bearing arranged in the centre accommodates the proportional weight of the rotor shaft. Depending on the direction of the ship's motion the spherical roller thrust bearings accommodate the propeller thrust/pull. To keep the rolling contact in each of the non­ loaded spherical roller thrust bearings the bearings are preloaded with springs via the housing washers. The rolling bearings are arranged in such a way that the slewing centres of all three bearings coincide and the required compensation of misalignment is thus achieved. The inner ring of the spherical roller bearing and the shaft washers of the spherical roller thrust bearings have a tight fit on the shaft. The outer ring of the spherical roller bearing has a floating fit in the housing and the housing washers of the spherical roller thrust bearings are radially relieved in the housing. The rolling bearings are heated in an oil bath during mounting and pushed onto the shaft. The bearings are dismounted hydraulically. For this, bores and annular grooves in the bearing seats are provided in the rotor shaft (see shaft end to dwg no. 175934/1.4). The piping leads from the bearing and the seal system via swivel up to the gravity tank (50 L) mounted at the highest point of the Azipod room. The oil level is at the tank. Inside the Azipod there is also a small tank with level alarm for monitoring seal system function. Filling of the propeller bearing space will be done from the 50 L gravity tank via OIL IN AND OUT line. Air is to be lead out via upper part of the gravity tank . Drainage ot the propeller bearing /is to be done by connecting pump 301 to one Azipod OIL IN AND OUT line at the time. Sensors, Automation At the propeller bearing there are two temp sensors T103 (connected to MAS) and T104 (to ABB drive control).They’ll give an ALARM at 90°C. Power reductions are made automatically according to following steps : 95°C 100°C 105°C 20% 40% 60%.

2/3 Total stop at 110°C . These temperature points can be changed later on, if oil type change or other reasons demand so. Level sensor LI02 (LAL) is at the gravity tank.lt is connected to MAS and will give an ALARM signal. From seal system there is one pipeline lead to the overflow tank just below the swivel.That tank is equipped with level sensor L107.lt is connected to MAS via slipring unit and it will give a SEAL SYSTEM OVERFLOW ALARM, if liquid level reaches it. Components and function Thrust bearing Thrust bearing unit is mounted to the aft end of the Azipod. It is filled with lub oil approximately to the center of the shaft. Sensors, Automation Temp sensors T101 (cap side) and T102 (motor side) are mounted at the thrust bearing. T101 is connected via slipring unit to MAS. T102 is connected via slipring unit to ABB drive control: Power reductions from thrust bearing oil temperature are made automatically according to following steps: 95 °C 20% 100°C 40% 105°C 60%. Total stop at 110°C . These temperature points can be changed later on, if oil type change or other reasons demand so. Level sensors L101 and L103(spare) are connected via slipring unit to MAS and will give a low level ALARM both.

ABB 3/3 Lub oil transfer pump For both Azipods there is an electric motor driven pump 400V, 50 Hz, 0.55 kW and a starter, located at the Azipod room. Ball valves are used for connecting the pump to the one Azipod piping system at the time for oil removal. A hose assembly is provided for connecting oil transfer pipelines at Azipod room by slipring unit to the Azipod internal piping(OIL IN AND OUT -lines). Piping arrangement contains stainless steel hydraulic precision tubes OD 18x1.5 and hydraulic fittings. Dimensioning The capacity of the pump is 10 litres/min of liquid (lub oil at T=40°C ) sucked from the shaft bearings which are 4.2 m below the pump.
